Welcome to Olga Primary School
Be the best you can be
Headteacher's Welcome
On behalf of all the children, staff and governors I would like to extend a warm welcome to our website and to our school. Olga is an inclusive, friendly school in the heart of the East End with an enviable location that enables us to take advantage of all that London has to offer. We are proud to be a community school and are lucky to have a rich mix of families from a huge variety of backgrounds.
Our values of being kind, being curious and being courageous are at the heart of what we do every day and underpins our motto of ‘be the best you can be.’ We strive to ensure that, whatever their starting point each child’s journey through Olga gives them the values, skills and knowledge to prepare them for each stage of their education and enables them to make a positive contribution to our local community and wider world.
Lisa Bradley-Jones, Headteacher
News
Weekly Update - 18th September 2026

pageCache.pageTitle: After School Clubs - Olga Primary School
pageCache.text:
After School Clubs
Early Birds Breakfast Club
Monday to Friday 8am-9am. Children must be dropped off by 8:45am if they wish to eat breakfast.
Open to all children attending school and only £3.00 per day.
Emergency/unplanned childcare (including breakfast) can also be arranged for parents who need to bring their child to school between 8-8:45am. This will be chargeable at £4.00 per session. Please book this via the Arbor app. You do not need to let the office know as your child's name will appear on the register once booked.
Night Owls After School Childcare Club
Monday to Friday from 3:20-6pm.
Open to all children attending school and charged at £10.00 per day. Snacks/food are included in the price.
Emergency after school childcare will also be offered to any parent of a child in the school and will be chargeable at £15.00 per session. Same day childcare is available if required. Please book this via the Arbor app. You do not need to let the office know as your child's name will appear on the register once booked.
How to Enrol in Early Birds / Night Owls
To enrol your child for Breakfast Club or Night Owls Childcare, you will need to download the Arbor app on your phone and book any sessions needed. If you use childcare vouchers to pay, please email Jenny@olga.towerhamlets.sch.uk to let us know before you book the sessions on the Arbor app as the system will request payment.
Note – If your child is new to Olga and starting in Nursery or Reception, they will not be able to start attending our childcare provision until they are settled and staying for the full school day.
After School Activity Clubs (Years 1-6 only)
The school runs after school activity clubs on most days from 3:30-4:30pm. Clubs rotate on a termly basis and are specific to year groups. Parents will be notified before the start of each new term which clubs will be on offer. Instructions on how to register for school clubs will be sent out prior to the clubs being released.
Note – Tax-Free Childcare and Childcare Vouchers are accepted for all wraparound care and after school activity clubs.

SEND
SEND Vision
At Olga Primary School we thrive to have a supportive inclusive environment, where high quality teaching is embedded in our practise, ensuring that children with additional needs are purposefully involved and making good progress for their learning journey.
We want all children to experience a rich and varied curriculum, based on enjoyable, hands on activities that provide them with deeper understanding and long-lasting experiences. We aim for children with additional needs to be taught alongside their peers ensuring they are an active participant.
We aim for children with additional needs to be identified as early as possible, including children joining our Early Years and new arrivals in different year groups.
We strongly believe that a team approach is key to children’s success in their journey through school. We aim for parents to act as partners, ensuring that their voice is heard, and they actively contribute to discussions around next steps and children’s targets.
We aim to create a strong and experienced network of support team around a child, by closely working with external professionals. Within the school day we recognise that every adult plays a vital role in ensuring a child’s success, and therefore we promote a culture of collaboration, discussion, and informed shared strategies.
By the time that children leave Olga Primary School we aim for all children, including those with additional needs to be confident and empowered learners who can communicate about their needs and how they learn best, recognising the power and impact of their own voice.

A person is regarded as having a disability under the Act where they have a physical or mental impairment that has a substantial and long-term adverse effect on their ability to carry out normal day-to-day activities.

French
"To learn a language is to have one more window from which to look at the world."
Intent
At Olga, our French curriculum aims to spark a love of language learning and nurture an appreciation of diverse cultures. We want our pupils to develop the confidence to communicate in French for real and practical purposes, both in speech and writing. By learning French, pupils gain more than vocabulary: they build resilience, problem-solving skills, and cultural awareness that broadens their horizons.
Our intention is to provide a strong foundation for language learning by:
In this way, our French scheme supports pupils to meet the Key Stage 2 attainment targets set out in the National Curriculum, while also fostering curiosity and passion for lifelong language learning.
Implementation
Our French curriculum is carefully structured around three interwoven knowledge strands which progress year on year, ensuring a secure accumulation of skills. The curriculum is organised as a spiral model: key vocabulary, grammar, and communication skills are revisited with increasing depth and complexity across the primary years.
Through clear progression of knowledge and skills, each unit builds systematically towards the end of Key Stage 2 expectations. Lessons are designed to provide balanced opportunities for spoken and written communication, with a strong focus on purposeful language use in familiar topics and real-life contexts.
Learning in French is practical, engaging, and varied:
Teaching is adaptive, creative, and inclusive, ensuring that every child is supported and challenged appropriately to make progress in their language journey.
Impact
The impact of our French curriculum is monitored continually through both formative and summative assessment. Teachers assess pupils’ progress against clear learning objectives, ensuring that knowledge and skills are securely embedded.

Ultimately, our pupils leave with the sense that learning a language is not just about words, but about broadening their perspective and opening new windows to the world.

Music
Intent
At Olga Primary School, children develop a love and understanding of music through listening, singing, performing, composing, recording, and evaluating music from a wide range of historical periods, styles, traditions, and genres.
Our aim is to nurture confident, creative musicians who are inspired to express themselves through music. We celebrate the diverse cultural heritages of our pupils by providing a broad variety of musical experiences throughout their time at Olga, including frequent performance opportunities.
We are committed to helping children recognise the value and importance of music within the wider community. Through developing their musical knowledge, skills, and experiences, pupils learn to engage with music in meaningful ways, both in school and beyond.
Implementation
At Olga Primary School, we follow the National Curriculum for Music, enriched by a bespoke programme designed to reflect the backgrounds, interests, and abilities of our pupils. The key areas of study are Listening, Performing, Composing, Recording, and Evaluating, all of which incorporate the core musical elements.
While all children work confidently within Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2 objectives, by Year 6 many are already progressing into Key Stage 3 areas of study. Our curriculum often takes a cross-curricular approach, complementing and extending learning in other subjects.
We adopt a global approach to music, drawing from a rich variety of musical cultures, including the children’s own family heritages, as well as contemporary works, historical periods, and world music. Music is also linked to key religious and cultural events throughout the year, such as Christmas, Eid, and Chinese New Year. This allows children to explore unfamiliar traditions while sharing their own musical backgrounds with peers.
From Nursery to Year 6, all children receive between 40 minutes and one hour of music each week. Reception to Year 6 use our dedicated music room, equipped with a wide range of percussive, acoustic, and electronic instruments. Each half term focuses on a different musical area, ensuring progressive development of skills and knowledge year by year.
Every Key Stage enjoys a weekly 25-minute singing assembly, where pupils learn, share, and perform songs from diverse genres and cultures. These sessions also support preparation for school performances, celebrations, and special events.
Throughout the year, selected year groups take part in special music projects and performances, such as the Border Crossings Opera Project and Seeds of Hope, a UNESCO-backed film project. We strive to ensure that every child experiences live performance opportunities during their time at Olga.
Instrumental Tuition:
Pupils are encouraged to work towards ABRSM (Associated Board of the Royal Schools of Music) exams and to participate in THAMES (Tower Hamlets Arts and Music Service) music days and the annual THAMES Celebration Concert.
Extra-Curricular Opportunities: We offer a range of free after-school music activities, including:
In addition to our whole-school Christmas Concerts, we host Spring and Summer Music Concerts, providing a wonderful opportunity for families to celebrate the children’s achievements and musical progress.
Year 3: Whole-class recorder lessons
Year 4: Whole-class violin tuition
Olga Orchestra (from Year 3 upwards)
Impact
Our Music Curriculum is designed to ensure clear progression of musical knowledge, skills, and confidence across all year groups. It enables pupils to explore and develop their own musical interests and strengths, fostering creativity, collaboration, and self-expression.
We measure impact through:
Ongoing discussions with children about their learning
Questioning and feedback within lessons

PE & Sports Premium
Sports Premium Funding
At Olga Primary School, we believe that sports and extra-curricular clubs play an important role in promoting social inclusion, healthy lifestyle and self-confidence, as well as helping children to discover and develop their talents and enthusiasms.
What is the Sports Premium?
From September 2014, the government has provided additional funding of £150 million per annum for academic year to improve provision of physical education (PE) and sport in primary schools.
Purpose of the funding
All schools have to spend the sport funding on improving their provision of PE and sport, but there is freedom to choose how we do it.
Our aim is to maintain and improve the quality and quantity of sports and afterschool clubs, inter and intra school competitions, and to increase the opportunities for pupils to try different activities whilst raising participation numbers.
At Olga Primary School we recognise the contribution of PE to the health and well-being of the children. We believe that an exciting and varied PE curriculum and extra-curricular opportunities have a positive influence on the concentration, attitude and academic achievement of all children. Furthermore, through sports and physical activity, we aim to reduce the incidence of obesity, smoking and other such activities which can have a detrimental impact upon pupil health and well-being.
Use of the funding at Olga Primary School
The money is use for the benefit of all children, regardless of their sporting ability. We will continue to place a high priority on our PE provision and to invest in staffing and resources to enhance the PE curriculum as well as extra-curricular sports and after schools clubs. In order to achieve our aims, the sports premium is used in the following ways:-

pageCache.pageTitle: Health and Wellbeing - Olga Primary School
pageCache.text:
Health and Wellbeing
At Olga our mission is to promote mental and physical health and wellbeing for all members of our school community – children, staff, parents, carers and governors. We put wellbeing at the heart of our school to ensure successful learning and to enable children to become the “best they can be”. We have a vision for whole-school well-being and a strategy for how we are going to drive that vision forward. Read all about our vision, strategy, other sources of support and our monthly ‘top tip’ by opening the tabs below and clicking the links.
Vision Statement and Accountability Framework
Our Vision Statement:
Mental health is: “the emotional and spiritual resilience which allows us to enjoy life and survive pain, disappointment and sadness. It is a positive sense of wellbeing and an underlying belief in our own, and others, dignity and worth.” (Mental Health First Aid England, 2017)
At Olga our mission is actively to promote positive mental health and wellbeing for our whole school community - children, staff, parents, carers and governors. We put wellbeing at the heart of our school to ensure successful learning and to enable children to become the “best they can be”.
Olga has a whole school inclusive approach. We recognise that we have both a moral and a legal duty to create a safe and calm, but stimulating, environment which enables pupils to be resilient and foster better mental health and wellbeing.
We help everyone in our community to understand what can affect our mental health. We foster an open and non-judgmental culture in which everyone is free to speak openly about mental health (“it’s ok not to be ok”) and is able access the right help if and when they need it.
We make sure that everyone has the opportunity to reach their full potential, building healthier and more positive relationships and staying safer both physically and mentally. We provide a structured school environment with clear processes and systems for identifying possible mental ill health and providing excellent mental health support, understanding and early intervention.
We have clear expectations of behaviour and systems to make sure that children succeed emotionally as well as academically.
Olga Accountability Framework
Well-being Champions
We have appointed eight wellbeing ambassadors across years 5 and 6 who will be available at lunch to lend support and a sympathetic ear to any children who are feeling upset, alone or just need some time to relax and unwind.
Our ambassadors will also be promoting wellbeing across the school, while being role models for treating their peers in a respectful and caring manner.
Over the next few years, we plan to expand the wellbeing ambassadors program across all year groups, allowing every child the opportunity to talk about their feelings with their peers and ensure that every child has the best playtime and lunchtime possible.
Organisations to support wellbeing and mental health:
Healthy Lives Team
The HEALTHY LIVES TEAM supports schools, pupils and families with everything to do with health and wellbeing. We want to help you live fitter, healthier and happier lives.
https://www.towerhamlets.gov.uk/lgnl/education_and_learning/The_Healthy_Lives_Team/The_Healthy_Lives_Team.aspx
Early Hub - Tower Hamlets
The Early Help Hub works with families or young people who would like some extra support to deal with a difficult situation. Getting help early can stop things from getting worse and becoming harder to manage.
https://www.towerhamlets.gov.uk/lgnl/health__social_care/children_and_family_care/Early_Help/Early_Help_Hub.aspx
Talking Therapies (Tower Hamlets)
Talking Therapies or psychological therapies are effective and confidential treatments delivered by fully trained and accredited NHS practitioners. They can help with common mental health problems like stress, anxiety and depression. You can access talking therapies for free on the NHS with a referral from your G.P or a G.P can refer you. They are open and accepting referrals, If you want to refer yourself, please use our online self-referral form or call 020 8475 8080.
Anna Freud National Centre for Children and Families
Parents and Carers resources offer advice and guidance to help support the children and young people who may be struggling with poor mental health.
YoungMinds are a mental health charity for children and have lots of practical advice and tips on supporting your child - from how to encourage your child to open up about their feelings to dealing with mental health services.
www.youngminds.org.uk
Parenting comes with lots of challenges, which can be even more difficult if you're dealing with wellbeing problems.
Mental health charity to make sure no one has to face a mental health problem alone.
Action for Happiness
Action for Happiness is a movement of people committed to building a happier and more caring society with lots of resources, events that will inspire you. There is also an app.
www.actionforhappiness.org
Mental Health Foundation
Mental health charity to make sure no one has to face a mental health problem alone.
https://www.mentalhealth.org.uk/
Apps
Try Headspace for free · Stress less with hundreds of meditations · Unwind with sleep sounds and music · Get in the zone with Focus music. There may be a cost after free trial.
https://www.headspace.com
Calm is an app for sleep and meditation 7 day free trail and a monthly charge to follow
Bright Sky is a free to download, confidential mobile app providing support and information for anyone who may be in an abusive relationship or those concerned about someone they know.

Health and Well-being monthly tip - https://www.nhs.uk/every-mind-matters/mental-wellbeing-tips/top-tips-to-improve-your-mental-wellbeing/
Why Is Sleep Important?
Sleep is important because it can help us physically heal, recover from illness, deal with stress, solve problems, consolidate memories, and improves motor skills, all contributing factors to improve our mental health. A good night’s sleep isn’t just about how many hours of sleep you get, but also the quality of that sleep. There are two essential kinds of sleep: non-rapid eye movement sleep (NREM) and rapid eye movement sleep (REM). NREM sleep helps your body wind down and fall into a deep sleep, which allows you to feel more rested in the morning. NREM sleep can help us physically heal, recover from illness, deal with stress, and solve problems. NREM sleep also plays a role in memory consolidation and can help boost the immune system. REM sleep bolsters learning and memory. REM sleep affects your mood, memory, and learning efficiency. Getting enough REM sleep can improve recall and memory consolidation and help your brain regulate the synapses associated with some types of motor learning. REM sleep is the sleep phase closest to wakefulness, and where most of our dreaming occurs. To find out more about our monthly topic of sleep, click on the following TED talk: https://www.ted.com/talks/matt_walker_sleep_is_your_superpower?language=en
How can you work towards protecting your mental health and well-being online?
Social media and the internet in general is an amazing way of keeping in touch with friends and letting them know what you’re up to. There are plenty of positives to focus on but it’s also important to consider how overuse of social media or exposure to offensive content can negatively affect your mental health. It’s important to protect your mental health online. This is not just the case for the pupils and children of Olga Primary School, this is a relevant topic for parents, teachers and pupils that spend any time on apps like Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and Tiktok. Nobody is guaranteed protection from being exposed to content online that impacts health and well-being. For more information please check out: https://www.themix.org.uk/mental-health/looking-after-yourself/protect-mental-health-online-23016.html#:~:text=Online%20coping%20strategies&text=Focus%20on%20connecting%20with%20people,that%20make%20you%20feel%20good.
https://www.ted.com/talks/peachy_liv_how_to_protect_your_mental_well_being_online_from_a_gen_zer
How is a growth mindset beneficial to your health and well-being?
Growth mindset is a fundamental focus within the policies that Olga Primary school create. This idea is not just useful for the work that our wonderful pupils put so much effort into, it can also benefit our health on a day to day basis.
A person with a growth mindset believes that every element of their mental and cognitive abilities can be developed at any stage of their life, and their current abilities are only a starting point. With effort, learning and persistence, everything can be challenged and people start to grow within themselves. When you have a fixed mindset, you have a hunger for approval, but when you have a growth mindset, you have a hunger for learning. Which mindset do you think is going to get you further in life AND help you be happier? If you would like to learn more about how a growth mindset can benefit your health and well-being, below there is a link to a blog and a TED talk. Don't just listen to us, listen to the professionals...... https://nutritionbycarrie.com/2020/10/growth-mindset.html https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hiiEeMN7vbQ

Home Learning & Remote Learning
At Olga, we refer to homework as “home learning”.​
As a parent or carer, you play a vital role in your child’s education and that includes supporting their home learning.
The Importance of Home Learning
Learning at home is an essential part of a good education. Regular home learning allows children to practise and reinforce what they have learned in class, helping them to develop key skills and make steady progress. It also encourages independence and confidence in their learning qualities that benefit them throughout school and later in life.
Home learning activities form an important part of our home–school partnership. All children are expected to take part in the range of home learning tasks set.
How Home Learning Works at Olga
Daily and Weekly Home Learning Tasks
Reading – All Year Groups​
From Nursery onwards, children bring books home to share with their parents or carers.
In Reception, children begin to bring home short reading books with a few words. They will have read these books three times in school, so they should be able to read them confidently at home.
Across the school, children will take home books matched to their reading ability. In addition, each child will also bring home a book that is beyond their reading level one for parents to read aloud and enjoy together.
As children grow older, they should read for at least 20 minutes each evening. Reading aloud with an adult remains valuable throughout primary school. Even fluent readers benefit from discussing the story for example, talking about the characters, language choices and key events.​
We ask parents and children to record their reading in the child’s reading diary.
Phonics – Early Years and Key Stage 1​
Children at the early stages of reading should regularly practise the sounds and tricky words found at the front of their reading books. We also ask that the Little Wandle books are read each night. Supporting materials are available to help you with this.
Spellings – Years 1 to 6​
From Year 1 onwards, children are given a set of spellings to learn each week. A few minutes of daily practice is far more effective than trying to learn them all at once.​ Spellings are carefully sequenced across the school. In Key Stage 1, they are linked to the phonics currently being taught.
Remote Learning
We will use remote learning if your child is unable to attend school due to illness or, in exceptional circumstances, during a partial or full school closure.
Our Remote Learning Platform
We use Google Classroom to share learning activities and resources.
What to Expect
Our Expectations for Parents and Pupils
To ensure the best possible remote learning experience, we ask that you:
Monitoring Engagement and Providing Feedback;
We are committed to ensuring every pupil can access remote education.​
If you do not have a suitable device or internet access, please contact the school office so that we can arrange alternative options such as printed work packs or a loaned device.

Art
"Every child is an artist. The problem is how to remain an artist once we grow up."
Intent
At Olga, we believe Art plays a vital role in nurturing pupils’ creativity, imagination, and self-expression, while also supporting social interaction, collaboration, fine motor development, and emotional wellbeing. Through Art, pupils learn to appreciate and interpret what they observe, communicate what they think and feel, and bring to life what they imagine and invent. At its best, Art is both intellectually stimulating and creatively demanding, offering every child the opportunity to express themselves and explore the world through a different lens.
Our aims for teaching Art are to enable pupils to:
Through these aims, we inspire children to develop as confident young artists with a deep appreciation of creativity, culture, and innovation.
Implementation
Our Art curriculum at Olga Primary School is carefully sequenced, ensuring progression of knowledge, skills, and vocabulary from the Early Years through to Year 6. Each year, pupils study at least three different artists and explore a wide variety of mediums, techniques, and outcomes, allowing them to build a rich portfolio of ideas and experiences.
The curriculum is structured around key strands, including:
Throughout their primary journey, pupils encounter “the great artists” highlighted in the National Curriculum such as Monet, Matisse, Frida Kahlo, and Picasso. They explore these artists’ work in depth and experiment with creating in similar styles across different media. Pupils also study diverse and local artists, such as Anish Kapoor, creator of the Orbit sculpture in Stratford, and Hafza Yusuf, a Somali clothes designer who has worked closely with the school to inspire pupils and came in to visit our school and see the art produced by the year 4 children.
By visiting art galleries and exhibitions across London, children are immersed in rich cultural experiences, seeing artwork first-hand and broadening their appreciation that art is not only something studied but a living, evolving form of expression all around us.

Computing
“The spread of computers and the Internet will put jobs in two categories. People who tell computers what to do, and people who are told by computers what to do.”
– Marc Andreessen, Entrepreneur, inventor of Netscape and member of the World Wide Web Hall of Fame.
At Olga we aim to give our children every opportunity to be in the first category.
Intent
Through the teaching of computing and online safety at Olga, children are encouraged to safely use computational thinking and creativity to understand and change the world. The children learn new computing and online safety specific knowledge and skills, and apply existing ones from a variety of disciplines, in particular mathematics, science and design and technology – all subjects that computing has deep links with. The knowledge and skills learned in computing are also applied across the entire curriculum.
Computing is split into three strands:
Implementation
EYFS
In the Early Years, technology is taught and used across the whole curriculum. Children recognise that a range of technology is used in places such as homes and schools and that online safety is important. The children are helped to be curious about technology in real world contexts through role-play and natural discussions. They learn to select and use technology for particular purposes across various areas of learning. A wide range of digital technologies (for example, iPads and programmable robots to support early coding skills) allow the children to represent their own ideas, thoughts and feelings -often collaboratively- as well as providing them with new ways to communicate and share their ideas. Within the EYFS we encourage parents to be involved in their child’s learning journey by using digital technology to record and share their child’s learning at home through photographs and videos taken on phone and iPads. We ensure there is a careful balance between encouraging parents to use digital technology with their children and understanding that there is a need to limit screen time so that its use is purposeful and meaningful. They develop skills such as investigating, evaluating, using commands and simple algorithms.
Years 1-6
In years 1-6 the core of computing is computer science; pupils are taught principles of information and computation, how digital systems work, and how to put this knowledge to use through programming. Building on this knowledge and understanding, pupils are equipped to use information technology to create programs, systems and a range of content. Computing also ensures that pupils become digitally literate –able to use, and express themselves and develop their ideas through information and communication technology- at a suitable level for the future workplace and as active participants in a digital world.
We follow the Teach Computing Curriculum.
Teach Computing
Teach Computing has been fully adapted so that it fits with our context in terms of overall curriculum aims and our equipment and software. It ensures that children receive the breadth of learning required by the National Curriculum, and that skills and knowledge are built on over time.
Units for each year group cover:
These things are taught through a range of projects that mean the children are encouraged to learn computing in a ‘real world’ joined up way, as opposed to learning discrete skills in isolation.
Please note we have a separate page on our website that details our approach to Online Safety.

Geography
“The study of geography is about more than just memorising places on a map. It’s about understanding the complexity of our world, appreciating the diversity of cultures that exist across continents. And in the end, it’s about using all that knowledge to help bridge divides and bring people together.”
Intent
At Olga Primary School, our Geography curriculum is designed to inspire pupils to be curious about the world and its people, fostering a lifelong fascination with diverse cultures, environments, and global connections. We encourage children to develop as kind and respectful global citizens, recognising their place in the world at local, national, and global scales. Our curriculum empowers them to be courageous thinkers who understand how people and the environment interact and how their actions can shape a sustainable future.
Our Geography curriculum covers all strands of the National Curriculum:
We enrich learning by actively using our local area, embracing Mile End’s rich diversity of landscapes, cultures, and communities. From investigating local parks and waterways to studying London’s dynamic urban environment, pupils apply classroom learning to real-life experiences that deepen their understanding and sense of place.
Our Geography teaching honours the diverse cultural heritages of our pupils. By drawing on their personal geographies and lived experiences, we provide a platform for sharing stories and perspectives, helping children see how their connections to people and places contribute to the wider human tapestry.
Through this approach, pupils build robust geographical knowledge and skills, develop kindness and respect for cultural diversity, cultivate curiosity about sustainability, and gain the courage to participate actively in an interconnected, evolving world.
Implementation
At Olga Primary School, we follow the National Curriculum for Geography, enhanced by a bespoke curriculum tailored to the local context and the backgrounds of our children. This ensures lessons are both meaningful and engaging, while broadening pupils’ horizons by exploring areas of the world they may not yet know.
Each year group explores three Geography units per academic year, with lessons delivered for one hour per week across three half terms. This structure promotes consistent, in-depth learning and helps pupils make meaningful connections across topics.
We bring Geography to life through enriched learning experiences, including educational visits and fieldwork. Each class participates in multiple visits a year, many directly linked to the Geography curriculum. Living in London offers exceptional opportunities to explore diverse environments—from local parks and waterways to the city’s unique urban landscape—providing real-world contexts that support and extend classroom learning.
We are committed to demonstrating clear progression across the school. Knowledge and skills are carefully sequenced to build year on year, supporting pupil development from Early Years through Key Stage 2. Each new unit and lesson begins with a recap of previous learning, linking new concepts to existing knowledge and helping pupils build a secure and connected understanding over time.
Through this thoughtfully structured and responsive curriculum, pupils at Olga develop confident geographical skills, deepen their understanding of the relationships between people and places, and grow as kind, curious, and courageous learners prepared to engage as thoughtful citizens at local, national, and global levels.

History
“The more you know about the past, the better prepared you are for the future.”
Intent
At Olga Primary School, our History curriculum aims to ignite pupils’ curiosity about the past and its impact on the present and future. We want children to develop a strong understanding of significant historical events, people, and periods, nurturing their ability to think critically, ask questions, and make meaningful connections across time.
As an anti-racist school, our curriculum actively challenges prejudice and inequality by celebrating diverse histories and perspectives. We ensure that pupils learn about the contributions and experiences of a wide range of cultures and communities, fostering respect, empathy, and a commitment to social justice.
Our intent is for pupils to:
By cultivating a passionate, informed, and inquisitive approach to history, we prepare children to become responsible, reflective, and anti-racist citizens who understand the importance of equality and inclusion in society today.
Implementation
At Olga Primary School, we implement the History curriculum through a carefully planned and sequenced spiral approach that builds pupils’ knowledge and skills progressively from Early Years through to Year 6. Our curriculum is designed to revisit key historical concepts and themes in increasing depth and complexity, allowing pupils to reinforce prior learning while making new connections across different periods and topics.
Each year group focuses on distinct historical units, structured to develop understanding of local, British, and world history. Lessons are planned to ensure that knowledge is broken down into manageable steps with clear learning objectives. This thoughtful sequencing supports pupils to build a secure foundation of historical knowledge that accumulates year on year.
Our curriculum places strong emphasis on historical enquiry and critical thinking. Pupils engage with a range of primary and secondary sources, learning to interpret evidence, ask questions, and construct their own informed narratives about the past. This process encourages curiosity, reflection, and an appreciation of diverse perspectives.
To bring history to life and deepen understanding, we incorporate visits, artefact exploration, and immersive activities wherever possible. Our teaching also includes deliberate opportunities for pupils to explore histories and cultures from underrepresented groups, reflecting our commitment to being an anti-racist school and promoting inclusivity.
Through this structured, progressive, and inclusive approach, pupils develop a deep and lasting understanding of history, preparing them to be thoughtful, informed, and respectful citizens.

Early Years and Foundation Stage
“Play is the highest form of research” - Albert Einstein
Welcome to Olga’s Early Years Foundation Stage
The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) at Olga Primary School includes Nursery (Cherry Class) and Reception (Lime and Orange Classes).
The Early Years provide the essential foundation for your child’s learning journey, a time when they develop the knowledge, skills, and confidence that will help them get the very best start in life.
At Olga, we are committed to creating a nurturing, safe, and happy environment where children can thrive. We know that children’s wellbeing is at the heart of all learning, and we strive to ensure every child feels valued, supported, and inspired to reach their full potential.
“Children learn and develop at a faster rate from birth to five years old than at any other time in their lives, so their experiences in early years have a major impact on their future life chances.” - Early Years Foundation Stage Statutory Framework, GOV.UK
Our setting offers a stimulating, imaginative, and engaging learning environment filled with inspiring opportunities. We encourage exploration and creativity through the use of open-ended and natural resources, helping to spark curiosity and a love of learning.
The Early Years Framework
The EYFS is built around seven areas of learning and development, all of which are interconnected and equally important.
The Prime Areas
These three areas form the foundation for all learning and are crucial for building relationships and developing key life skills:
Communication and Language
Physical Development
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
The Specific Areas
The four specific areas strengthen and extend the prime areas, igniting children’s curiosity and enthusiasm for learning:
Literacy
Mathematics
Understanding the World
Leading to History, Geography, Science, and R.E.
Expressive Arts and Design
Leading to Art, Music and Design Technology
Olga’s EYFS Curriculum
At Olga, we follow the Early Years Framework alongside Development Matters to guide the learning, development, and care of every child.
Our curriculum takes a holistic approach, focusing on both the Prime and Specific Areas while incorporating the essential foundational knowledge that children need to reach their potential.
Language and Communication
Language development sits at the heart of our EYFS curriculum. Some children join us with a rich vocabulary and are challenged through creative, ambitious language experiences. Others begin their journey with English as an additional language or specific speech and language needs. Our curriculum is carefully structured to support every child, using language-rich texts, stories, and activities across all areas of learning.
We ensure our children encounter a diverse range of poems, songs, and stories that reflect their own lives and the rich diversity of our community. Representation matters and we want every child to see themselves and their families reflected in our books, resources, visitors, and experiences.
Learning Environment and Continuous Provision
Our EYFS environment is thoughtfully designed to support the curriculum and promote creative, meaningful play-based learning. Through continuous provision, children demonstrate their knowledge and understanding, becoming ‘experts’ in different areas of the setting.
Open-ended resources encourage curiosity, creativity, and critical thinking. For example, our construction and block play areas in Nursery and Reception help children develop concepts of balance, space, shape, measure, and stability.
Alongside continuous provision, planned enhancements enrich play and introduce new learning opportunities to extend children’s thinking.
Individualised Learning
We understand that equality does not mean sameness, and each child’s learning journey is unique. Our planning reflects this through personalised teaching, targeted interventions, parent and carer workshops, and enriching educational experiences.
We strongly believe in learning through play, balanced with carefully structured lessons that support the teaching of key knowledge and skills. Our play-based curriculum is designed around the unique child, ensuring learning is joyful, purposeful, and developmentally appropriate.
Please see below for the yearly overviews for both Nursery and Reception. This sets out the key knowledge, texts, and “Big Ideas” explored throughout the year.
Olga’s EYFS Curriculum Rationale
Children join Olga Primary from a wide range of backgrounds and starting points. Our EYFS curriculum is designed to remove barriers to learning and give every child an equal opportunity to succeed.
We maintain a strong focus on communication, language, and high-quality texts, ensuring our teaching reflects and celebrates the diversity of our community.
Our curriculum carefully balances:
Foundational knowledge for wider curriculum subjects in Key Stage 1 and 2 is organised under ‘Big Ideas’, which connect the EYFS Framework, Early Learning Goals, and the National Curriculum, helping children make meaningful links in their understanding.
Educational Visits and Experiences
We believe that real-life experiences are a vital part of learning. Our children enjoy a wide range of educational visits and visitors that bring learning to life, from exploring local community spaces to discovering London’s landmarks.
Typical visits and experiences include:
We also welcome visitors such as dentists, doctors, and artists, who share their expertise, inspire curiosity and open our children’s eyes to possibilities.
